incidents.cause: The student pilot's improper flare and improper recovery from a bounced landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain pitch control during the landing, resulting in a porpoise.
an inadvertent encounter with birds during approach to land that resulted in substantial damage.
The right nose landing gear axle's failure from intergranular and fatigue cracking due to an earlier bearing failure.
The failure of the right main landing gear inboard axle due to fatigue cracking as a result of fretting damage in one of the brake mounting bolt holes.
An in-flight encounter with turbulence during cruise flight, which resulted in a serious injury to a flight attendant.
The A340 captain's failure to maintain adequate clearance between his wing and the tail of the EMB-145.
The improper air traffic control takeoff clearance issued by the local controller because of his lack of monitoring and lack of awareness of the conflicting arrival airplane.
An in-flight collision with a bird during the descent to land, which resulted in substantial damage to the airplane.

The airport authorities' improper decision to deactivate the jet bridge braking system which created an unsafe condition by the gate agents not being able to stop the bridge from impacting the airplane during a wind gust.
an inadvertent fall out of the open service door because the safety strap was not attached.
The pilot's failure to see and avoid wires while maneuvering at a low-altitude, which resulted in the main rotor blades striking the wires.
The premature failure of one of the No. 2 engine compressor bleed valve, which resulted in a partial loss of power to that engine.
The pilot’s loss of directional control during engine start.
An in-flight fire that resulted from an inadequate 100-hr inspection, which failed to detect and correct improper electrical cable routing in the engine compartment.
